metadata.goal: Analyze the provided trajectories within a common area and identify how their movement characteristics vary across time periods.
metadata.dataset_description: 64 constructed vehicle trajectories across four days in one South Brooklyn road corridor. All point geometries are forward subroutes of the cached OSRM road polyline; timestamps are integrated from segment distances and endpoint speeds. Detour score is route distance divided by endpoint great-circle distance. Context and speed profiles are constructed; these are not original GPS observations.
metadata.header: WorldTrace Time-Conditioned Mobility in South Brooklyn

insight_list.insight: On cold days, more vehicle trajectories pass through the South Brooklyn area during daytime hours than during non-daytime hours.

plot.title: Cold-Day Vehicle Trajectory Start-Time Distribution
plot.description: Each point is one cold-day vehicle trajectory. Daytime and non-daytime trajectories use different colors, and horizontal lines show the mean start hour for each group; the point counts show the daytime concentration without using a bar chart.

insight_list.question: How are the start times of vehicle trajectories distributed between daytime and non-daytime hours on cold days?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use the daytime concentration as an observed temporal pattern for this area, without treating the temperature grouping as a causal explanation.
insight_list.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

cold = df[df["temperature_2m_c"] < 5].copy()
cold["period"] = np.where(cold["hour"].between(6, 18), "Daytime", "Non-daytime")
colors = {"Daytime": "#2563eb", "Non-daytime": "#f97316"}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
for x, period in enumerate(["Daytime", "Non-daytime"]):
 values = cold.loc[cold["period"] == period, "hour"].to_numpy()
 jitter = rng.normal(0, 0.055, size=len(values))
 ax.scatter(np.full(len(values), x) + jitter, values, color=colors[period], alpha=0.72, s=34, label=f"{period} (n={len(values)})")
 ax.hlines(values.mean(), x - 0.22, x + 0.22, color=colors[period], linewidth=3, label=f"{period} mean = {values.mean():.1f} h")
ax.set_xticks([0, 1], ["Daytime", "Non-daytime"])
ax.set_ylabel("Trajectory start hour")
ax.set_title("Cold-Day Vehicle Trajectory Start-Time Distribution")
ax.legend(frameon=False, ncol=2)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Afternoon trajectories usually have higher route-indirectness scores than trajectories in the other time periods.

plot.title: Route Indirectness across Time Periods

x_axis.name: Time period
x_axis.description: Midnight, morning, midday, afternoon, or evening based on trajectory start hour.

plot.description: The distribution view shows whether afternoon trajectories are generally more indirect rather than relying on one average.

insight_list.question: How does route indirectness vary across the time periods, and which period has the highest scores?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Treat the afternoon route-indirectness elevation as an observed time-of-day difference in this common area, not as proof of its cause.
insight_list.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

bins = [-1, 5, 10, 12, 17, 23]
labels = ["midnight", "morning", "midday", "afternoon", "evening"]
df = df.copy()
df["time_period"] = pd.cut(df["hour"], bins=bins, labels=labels)
df.boxplot(column="detour_score", by="time_period", grid=False)
plt.suptitle("")
plt.title("Route Indirectness across Time Periods")
plt.xlabel("Time period")
plt.ylabel("Route-indirectness score")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Trajectories in the morning and around midnight have much higher average speeds than trajectories in the other time periods.

insight_list.question: Which time periods have the highest average trajectory speeds, and how do they compare with the other periods?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use morning and midnight as the high-speed reference periods for this area when comparing time-of-day trajectory behaviour.
insight_list.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

bins = [-1, 5, 10, 12, 17, 23]
labels = ["midnight", "morning", "midday", "afternoon", "evening"]
df = df.copy()
df["time_period"] = pd.cut(df["hour"], bins=bins, labels=labels)
means = df.groupby("time_period", observed=False)["avg_speed_kmh"].mean().reindex(labels)
means.plot(kind="bar", color="seagreen")
plt.title("Average Speed across Time Periods")
plt.xlabel("Time period")
plt.ylabel("Mean average speed (km/h)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

insights: On cold days, more vehicle trajectories pass through the South Brooklyn area during daytime hours than during non-daytime hours.
Afternoon trajectories usually have higher route-indirectness scores than trajectories in the other time periods.
Trajectories in the morning and around midnight have much higher average speeds than trajectories in the other time periods.
summary: Across 64 vehicle trajectories in the same South Brooklyn area over four consecutive days, cold-day vehicle trajectories are more numerous during daytime hours, afternoon trajectories have the highest route-indirectness scores, and morning and midnight trajectories have the highest average speeds.

input_references.role: Complete timestamped road geometry and kinematics for all 64 trajectories
